title: Pointwise equality of two Real.morphisms into a model (Rmorph_uniq)
intent: Prove that there is at most one Real.morphism from a Real.structure S into a Real.model R, by showing any two such morphisms phi, psi agree pointwise in the setoid sense. The proof halves the work by symmetry (wlog), then rules out a strict separation psi x < phi x by interpolating a rational, which morphisms preserve and whose order they reflect.

parent.name: Rmorph_uniq
parent.statement:
Theorem Rmorph_uniq (S : Real.structure) (R : Real.model) (phi psi : S -> R) :
    Real.morphism phi -> Real.morphism psi ->
  pointwise_relation S Real.eq phi psi.

applicability.goal_shape: An equality of two functions phi, psi stated pointwise over a setoid equality that is order-antisymmetry: pointwise_relation S Real.eq phi psi, where phi and psi are both structure-preserving maps (Real.morphism) from a structure S into a model R.
applicability.use_when: the two maps preserve a dense subset (here the rationals ratR) and reflect the order (Real.morph_le), so a strict inequality between phi x and psi x pulls back to a contradiction; excluded middle is available in the model; and the statement is symmetric in the two maps, so wlog halves the work.
applicability.avoid_when: the codomain is only a Real.structure, not a Real.model (no excluded middle, no density); the maps do not reflect the order; the equality to prove is intensional (=) rather than the setoid Real.eq; or the two order directions need genuinely different arguments, so the wlog symmetry fails.

consequences: The move splits the pointwise equality into the two order directions and discharges both from a single wlog proof of phi x <= psi x. Obligations it creates: excluded middle must be available (reals_classic, derivable from the Real.sup_total axiom, so the codomain must be a Real.model); the rationals must be dense in the model (ratR_dense); and the morphism must both preserve the dense subset (Rmorph_rat) and reflect the order (Real.morph_le) to pull the interpolated rational back to a contradiction. Failure modes: the argument depends on the order being total so that ~(phi x <= psi x) is a strict psi x < phi x, and on the equality being the setoid Real.eq (order antisymmetry) rather than intensional =.
